events.title: Henry II and Bolesław I make the Peace of Bautzen
events.description: Emperor Henry II and Duke Bolesław I the Brave of Poland concluded the Peace of Bautzen, ending fifteen years of intermittent war over Lusatia, Meissen and Bohemia. Poland kept Lusatia and Milsko, and German knights later joined Bolesław's expedition to Kiev.

events.title: Wareru proclaims himself king of Martaban as Pagan collapses
events.description: Wareru, a Mon of humble origin, declared himself king of Martaban as the Pagan Kingdom collapsed, and Pagan, in its death throes, took no action. His kingdom, later called Hanthawaddy, ruled Lower Burma until 1539.

events.title: Charles I is beheaded in Whitehall
events.description: Convicted of treason, Charles I was executed on a scaffold outside the Banqueting House. England became a republic, and the monarchy was not restored until 1660.
events.html: Convicted of treason, Charles I was executed on a scaffold outside the Banqueting House. England became a republic, and the monarchy was not restored until 1660.

events.title: Andrew Jackson survives an assassination attempt
events.description: At the US Capitol, the house painter Richard Lawrence fired two pistols at Jackson, but both misfired. It was the first known attempt to kill a sitting American president.
events.html: At the US Capitol, the house painter Richard Lawrence fired two pistols at Jackson, but both misfired. It was the first known attempt to kill a sitting American president.

events.title: Yerba Buena is renamed San Francisco
events.description: Lt. Washington Allon Bartlett's proclamation renaming Yerba Buena as San Francisco took effect, months after US forces raised the American flag there in the Mexican–American War. The Gold Rush later made it the major city of the west coast.
events.html: Lt. Washington Allon Bartlett's proclamation renaming Yerba Buena as San Francisco took effect, months after US forces raised the American flag there in the Mexican–American War. The Gold Rush later made it the major city of the west coast.

events.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt is born at Hyde Park, New York
events.description: Roosevelt led the United States through the Great Depression and most of the Second World War. He is the only president elected four times.
events.html: Roosevelt led the United States through the Great Depression and most of the Second World War. He is the only president elected four times.

events.title: Hitler appointed Chancellor of Germany
events.description: President Hindenburg made the Nazi leader Chancellor, with conservatives expecting to control him. Within months Hitler had suspended civil liberties and established a one-party dictatorship.

events.title: Soviet submarine sinks the Wilhelm Gustloff
events.description: Torpedoes from submarine S-13 sank the overcrowded German liner in the Baltic as it evacuated refugees and military personnel. An estimated 9,000 died, the greatest loss of life in a single sinking.
events.html: Torpedoes from submarine S-13 sank the overcrowded German liner in the Baltic as it evacuated refugees and military personnel. An estimated 9,000 died, the greatest loss of life in a single sinking.

events.title: Mahatma Gandhi is assassinated in New Delhi
events.description: The Hindu nationalist Nathuram Godse shot Gandhi at a prayer meeting at Birla House. The death of the leader of India's non-violent independence struggle was mourned across the world.
events.html: The Hindu nationalist Nathuram Godse shot Gandhi at a prayer meeting at Birla House. The death of the leader of India's non-violent independence struggle was mourned across the world.

events.title: Tet Offensive begins in South Vietnam
events.description: North Vietnamese and Viet Cong forces attacked towns and bases across South Vietnam during the lunar new year truce. Though repelled, the offensive undermined American confidence in the war.

song: British; later the British Empire and the Commonwealth realms
The national anthem of the United Kingdom, a short prayer for the monarch first printed in 1744. Nobody knows who wrote it.
